_readme: Extensible table of real-world lab-pack category conventions, provided incrementally by the client (South Lake Environmental) as industry packing-protocol knowledge, distinct from the CFR-derived compliance screens in SKILL.md Step 3. Each entry is a named category a non-RCRA (or, for hardSegregate categories, ANY) item can belong to, with a join rule the segregation step (SKILL.md Step 4) applies when deciding whether an item can share an existing drum or must start/join a category-specific one. Add new rows as the client shares more categories — do not invent categories not explicitly given.

categories.label: Class 5.1 oxidizers
categories.rule: A DOT Class 5.1 (oxidizer) item is NEVER combined with any other material in any drum, regardless of RCRA status or general Appendix V compatibility. Contamination risk with organic material. Always its own drum, always.

categories.label: Class 5.2 organic peroxides
categories.rule: A DOT Class 5.2 (organic peroxide) item is always segregated by its own DOT UN number specifically — two different UN numbers within 5.2 do not share a drum even with each other, let alone anything else.
categories.joinCondition: only an item sharing the exact same UN number, never combined across different UN numbers or with any other class

categories.label: Toxic (6.1) organic liquids, PG II/III
categories.rule: Non-RCRA organic materials generally join a toxic (Division 6.1) PG II or PG III organic lab pack when one exists in the job.
categories.joinCondition: item is organic, non-RCRA (or RCRA-compatible per the normal Appendix V screen), and the job has an existing 6.1 PG II/III organic drum with room
categories.example: Methyl salicylate (2026-09-25 inventory) — non-RCRA organic ester; would join a toxic PG II/III organic drum if one existed in that job. None did, so it got its own drum by default, not because it's inherently un-poolable.

categories.label: Inorganic acids
categories.rule: Non-regulated inorganic materials generally join an inorganic-acid-compatible lab pack.
categories.joinCondition: item is inorganic and acid-compatible, and the job has an existing inorganic-acids drum with room
categories.example: Iodine crystals (2026-09-25 inventory) — inorganic, acid-compatible; would join an inorganic-acids drum if one existed in that job. None did, so it got its own drum by default.

categories.label: Inorganic bases / caustics
categories.rule: Non-regulated inorganic materials generally join an acid/base-compatible lab pack (base side of the same general category as inorganic_acid — do not combine the acid and base sub-groups with each other, same as the existing Appendix V 1-A/1-B pairing already in Step 4).
categories.joinCondition: item is inorganic and base-compatible, and the job has an existing inorganic-base drum with room

categories.label: Common salts
categories.rule: Common salts are flexible — generally placed in a toxic, acid, or non-haz lab pack depending on the specific salt's own hazard profile. Not a single fixed category; evaluate the specific salt against the other categories first (toxic_organic_pg2_3, inorganic_acid, inorganic_base, non_haz_general) and place accordingly.
categories.joinCondition: case-by-case per the salt's actual hazard characteristics; this row exists to flag salts as poolable rather than defaulting them to their own isolated drum

categories.label: Non-hazardous, general
categories.rule: The fallback category: a non-RCRA item with no better-matching category above (no compatible inorganic-acid/base drum, no toxic-organic drum, not a salt with a clearer home) goes into a general non-haz lab pack alongside any other item that also has no better category match, subject to the normal compatible-and-room test.
categories.joinCondition: item is non-RCRA, no more specific category above applies, and the job has an existing non-haz-general drum with room
